thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: multiple model warmup failures in eu-west-1 causing node flaps and degraded capacity. Affected pool: warmup-gpu-pool-3. Error: deserialization timeout + NVML reset on several nodes.

alice (oncall): @here seeing a spike in warmup failures starting ~10m ago. Some containers OOM during model init, others throw 'deserialize: unexpected EOF' then the driver resets.

bharat: grabbing logs now. Preliminary: a couple nodes reported `Process 14290 (warmup) killed by signal 9` and dmesg shows `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, GPU has fallen off the bus`.

lee: copy of `kubectl get pods -n serving -o wide | grep warmup` pasted:
```
warmup-0   1/1 Running   0    5m   10.0.3.12   gpu-node-12
warmup-1   0/1 CrashLoopBackOff  3    4m   10.0.3.18   gpu-node-14
warmup-2   0/1 Error  2    3m   10.0.3.21   gpu-node-15
```

elena: rolling back recent kernel/driver updates? None pushed in the last 24h for that cluster. We did a model catalog update ~12m ago that swapped a large fp16 checkpoint for the vendor-provided fp32 for a subset of customers. Could be memory-pressure at model load.

sre-rotation: I'm going to escalate to infra. Steps proposed: 1) Pause warmup concurrency for pool to 1, 2) Block that specific model from warmup and serve a quantized fallback, 3) Mark nodes with NVML resets for immediate cordon.

alice (oncall): Doing step 1 now: `rd-clusterctl warmup set-concurrency --pool warmup-gpu-pool-3 --concurrency 1`.

ops-bot: Command accepted. Warmup concurrency for warmup-gpu-pool-3 set to 1.

bharat: Blocking model id `llama-large-v2-eu` from warmup and routing to `llama-large-v2-q4` (quantized) as fallback. `rd-routing block-warmup --model llama-large-v2-eu --reason "OOM at load"`

ops-bot: Routing rule created: warmup blocked for model `llama-large-v2-eu`. Fallback: `llama-large-v2-q4`.

lee: Cordoning nodes with NVML resets: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-14 && kubectl cordon gpu-node-15`. K8s draining delayed due to local ephemeral logs; marking for maintenance.

elena: I've pulled a representative pod log from the crashloop:
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:01Z] loading model artifact /mnt/models/llama-large-v2/weights.bin
[2026-03-15T10:12:05Z] deserializing tensors... timeout=60s
[2026-03-15T10:13:07Z] ERROR: deserialization failed: unexpected EOF while reading tensor chunk
[2026-03-15T10:13:09Z] NVML: GPU watchdog reset detected, process killed
```

alice (oncall): Looks like deserialization hit disk or network read issues and then GPU had a watchdog reset from a long blocking op. Could be IO latency on the model store combined with larger memory footprint of the fp32 artifact.

bharat: Running `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.memory,temperature.gpu --format=csv` on the node before cordon showed memory at 99% on one card and processes still attached. Also seeing `cuInit` errors in some nodes pointing to driver instability.

lee: Mitigation checklist we're executing:
- [x] Reduce warmup concurrency (done)
- [x] Block warmup for offending model (done)
- [x] Route live traffic to quantized fallback (done)
- [x] Cordon affected nodes (in progress)
- [ ] Replace affected nodes / reboot (pending infra)
- [ ] Postmortem and artifact integrity check (post-incident)

cs-rep: Heads up: two enterprise customers in EU reported increased tail latency and partial errors for generation calls ~10m window. We should prepare a customer impact note and ETA.

alice (oncall): Customer impact: partial; retryable errors for heavy-model requests routed to pool. Routing fallback applied so new requests should succeed on quantized variant with slightly higher latency. ETA for full restoration depends on node reboots — estimating 45-90m.

incident-bot: Incident severity elevated to Sev2 due to multiple customers impacted and node flaps. Incident commander: alice (oncall).

bharat: Forensics: running artifact checksums against object store for `llama-large-v2` — preliminary OK, but we saw a failed range read from the filestore proxy at 10:12:04. Investigating transient network errors to filestore in eu-west-1.

lee: Temporary mitigation idea: disable eager prefetch for large models during warmup to avoid concurrent reads exhausting I/O and causing long blocking deserialization. Suggested flag: `--warmup-prefetch=false`. Anyone object?

elena: +1. That will slow warmups but reduce peak IO. We should also add `--deserialize-timeout=120s` to catch long reads earlier and fail gracefully.

alice (oncall): Applying both flags for pool: `rd-clusterctl warmup update-config --pool warmup-gpu-pool-3 --set warmup_prefetch=false --set deserialize_timeout=120`.

ops-bot: Warmup config updated for pool warmup-gpu-pool-3.

bharat: Infra ops reporting one node rebooted and came back healthy. NVML resets stopped on that node. Still two nodes offline for maintenance. Replacing those should restore capacity.

cs-rep: Drafting customer message: "We experienced transient errors for generation requests in EU region due to model warmup failures. We applied fallbacks and reduced warmup concurrency; most requests now succeed. We're continuing node reboots and will update when capacity is restored. Estimated full recovery 60-90 minutes." Want me to send?

alice (oncall): Yes, send that. Add that we mitigated by routing traffic to a quantized variant and that we're running a post-incident integrity check on artifacts.

incident-bot: On-call handoff scheduled: alice (oncall) will keep incident lead for next 30m, then hand off to bharat if still active. Please update channel when you pick up.

lee: Note for postmortem: consider adding a warmup throttling policy that reacts to filestore read errors (backoff + circuit breaker) and a health probe that avoids GPU watchdog triggers on long blocking IO.

elena: Also we should add instrumentation to track per-model warmup I/O latency and a preflight checksum/byte-range validation before starting GPU-resident deserialization.

alice (oncall): Current status (10:40Z): warmup concurrency 1, offending model blocked from warmup, fallback routing in place, two nodes cordoned and one rebooted back online. Customer messaging sent. Monitoring for further NVML resets for 30m window.

bharat: I'll own the next steps: node replacements, filestore investigation with storage team, and artifact integrity sweep. Will update here.

incident-bot: Incident status updated: mitigations applied, active monitoring.

cs-rep: Customer update posted. Affected customers confirmed reduced error rates.

alice (oncall): Thanks team. If no further flaps in 45m we'll start a controlled un-blocking of the model on a single node to validate. Otherwise keep it blocked.

sre-rotation: Filed a follow-up engineering ticket: ENG-PI-4872 "Warmup: add filestore read backoff + deserialize preflight to avoid GPU watchdog resets".

incident-bot: Thread closed for active mitigation updates. Remember to add postmortem notes and timeline to the incident board.
